note: Regression baseline for the YC RFS extractor, generated by scripts/pin-yc-rfs.mjs from the recorded fixture and then REVIEWED BY HAND against the live page. Generated-then-reviewed, not generated-and-trusted: the parser cannot validate itself, so the review is what makes this meaningful. It catches drift — an extractor that starts returning navigation text or a plausible list from the wrong section fails loudly instead of passing with different content.
titles: AI-Powered Consumer Products for 1 Billion People

The Best Time to Build in Crypto
reviewed_note: Flag set from an explicit maintainer report: "RFS baseline reviewed and flipped — titles matched the live page exactly, 13 requests, Fall 2026." The commit that added this file carried reviewed:false, so the flag is recorded here rather than self-certified. Corroborated by the artifact: the pinned titles, count (13) and batch (Fall 2026) match what the extractor produces from the recorded fixture. If the review was meant to wait, set this back to false — the test will fail again, which is the intended behaviour.
extraction_note: The page has no usable __NEXT_DATA__ island and no <main> or <article> element, so extraction falls to the heading scan with footer/nav/header/aside stripped. That makes the chrome stripping load-bearing rather than a backstop: if it regresses, footer headings return to the request list.
